topic: Facial attractiveness first impressions — evidence review, not a publication approval
reviewerMethod: Directly opened and read original publisher full-text HTML of both studies; separately compared to an existing AI-generated draft.

sources.title: Anchoring has little effect when forming first impressions of facial attractiveness
Forming impressions of facial attractiveness is mandatory

claims.claim: In the sequential-photo task, descending versus ascending images differed by about 0.22 points on a 1–7 attractiveness scale in the first experiment.
claims.basis: Publisher full-text abstract, experiments, and general discussion. Experiment 1 recruited 301 participants.
claims.limitations: Experimental ratings of selected celebrity photographs; the study did not establish an effect on real-world romantic or employment decisions.

claims.claim: The authors did not detect a significant difference between randomly ordered and ascending/descending photograph sequences in experiment 2.
claims.basis: Publisher full-text abstract and Experiment 2 (n=307), compared against Experiment 1 ordering groups.
claims.limitations: Absence of a detected difference within this design does not prove all first impressions are freely controllable.

claims.claim: While learning faces for an identification task, observers still developed attractiveness impressions that influenced later ratings of middle-attractiveness photographs.
claims.basis: Original 2017 full text, abstract and three experimental findings.
claims.limitations: Experimental photograph learning, not a longitudinal or everyday relationship study. Automatic impression formation does not prove lifelong permanence.

claims.claim: A person can reliably manipulate any first impression simply by presenting photographs in a planned order.
claims.basis: The original study found only a small difference and no convincing real-world evidence.
claims.limitations: Do not state as practical advice or verified effect.

claims.claim: Initial facial attractiveness impressions are permanent and cannot be changed by later information or interactions.
claims.basis: The original study examined difficulty suppressing impressions within experimental conditions, not lifetime permanence.

articleAssessment.verifiedCoverage: Only the specified claims, figures and boundaries above were independently checked.
articleAssessment.reason: The existing Notion draft is not identical to a vetted public-only candidate. Article wording, completeness, privacy, copyright, image rights and audience value have not passed the existing publication gate.
articleAssessment.requiresNext: Create a public-safe source-aligned candidate with no private facts, verify its claims one by one, pass the GitHub editorial gate and review before publication.
